what they call revolution, in some parts of Africa, and mainly Central Africa and West Africa. I worked since 2006 on this phenomena with teams of researchers. I was happy to get some grants. So the work I present is the result of work of PhDs, master's students, etc., for almost an hour.

12 years, yes. So I'm quite an empirical person, working in the field close to people, listening to people, and theory is not my biggest issue, but I try. This title, The Empire of the Digital, The Empire, Why the Empire of the Digital, is an inspiration of a workshop we organized in Nairobi, where the question was, do we indeed see a new kind of empire?

Westerns see as positive. There are also movements that we really discussed, which is the radicalization and jihadi kind of movements. But these are of a similar process. It's the influence people have through mobile telephony, through social media, through communication that makes people choose for a different, maybe, direction in their lives.

while doing research on mobile communities. So we did a research on how Cameroonians relate to Cameroonians, from Cameroon relate to Cameroonians who live in South Africa, who live in Germany. And the whole ritual and everything will be not only paid for by this whole diaspora community, but they will also all receive instant videos from the burial in Bamenda. So you can see that this is a community living with each other, but spread all over the world. And the interesting thing is, this is a name-giving ceremony of a baby in South Africa.

with the Cameroon attire of a specific ethnic group. the capital city of Cameroon, showing the government asking for getting control of that digital empire back again. And they didn't manage. But that's the other story for the coming few years. In 2012, the first big movement was happening, I think, in Senegal, and clearly organized through mobile telephony. Combined with short messages on Facebook, this works really as a catalysator and as a sort of an explanation of what things,

are happening. It is also, and you all know this, a way to get things out that normally do not come out. So in Chad, with the coming elections in 2016, the period... as you can see, violated by the military, this could no longer be contained because it went viral. This is very interesting because those kind of moments of getting news out had a huge effect on the mobilization of youth in the streets, and this is then the protest in peace by youth in Chad that could never have happened before.

In this case, it didn't lead to a big movement because the authoritarian regime that DB has put in place, DB is the president, didn't shy away from these facts and was able, despite the presence of French and all the international community, to just oppress the population and nothing is happening. Since a year...

access to internet is impossible in this country. But it did do something, and society is changing. And there are different discussions among the youth. And this can lead to new forms of mobilization of youth to protest, which is happening in Congo, which is happening a little bit in Cameroon.

which did happen in Senegal and in Burkina Faso. In Burkina Faso and in Senegal, they were able to send away presidents and replace them by others. So this could never have happened, I argue, without the new access to mobile telephony. And these are forms of resistance that come up in this digital empire that are difficult to control, except when you have a very harsh iron fist.

And these iron fists can only exist if the world allows them to exist. And that's us. So then the last thing that I want to highlight is this M radicalization. We talk a lot about radicalization. change their thinking and go over to another ideology of the world and embrace this as the real way to go forward. So it happens somewhere there is information and information becomes something when you appropriate it.

For the people who live in Central Mali, that's the area where I worked for a long time and follow people already 25 years, they discovered through this war a new discourse which came through preaches of jihadi leaders in their phones in which they were sort of, they were explained that their situation in their society has always been

the position of the underdog. It sounds a bit strange maybe, but to see that, someone has to tell you. Someone has to explain you. When you didn't go to school, someone has to explain you how this works. This happened when this war entered Mali and when these jihadists occupied some areas.

starting to explain people how the world works and how they were always exploited. I explain now very quickly, but that's a bit what happened. This man...

problems going on they are searching for new ways at that moment that this opening is there these groups from jihadi i call them now jihadi groups come with a very good way of using social media and information flows explaining those people that maybe you need to do something else with your life than just following your elites then the state leaves the area because it's becoming very

So they did invite some of the government people there. But this was organized all through mobile phone.

So they called each other and they all came and they united and there were thousands of nomads who normally do not flock together like this. sharing of ideas that we would call radical, organization of a kind of a hybrid. These boys are just herding their cattle, but with a Kalashnikov today. I think this is a development, the change of the mindset, then the change of organization.

The redefinition of your position in society, in a world in which they grew up, in which there was hardly any Western education, a little bit of Muslim education, a long history of heroism, of pastoralism, and then after independence, a history of neglect, leads these people, due to information they receive through their mobile phones,

amongst others now WhatsApp, with audio messages, so you don't need to write or read, but you access a lot of information through audio, and it unites them. So they are a group of people who we could say part of something that is M radicalization. So the M ethnicity, the M movement, and the M radicalization are of course parts of the same processes,

But they were never expected. And they do redefine our world in interesting ways, I think. And they also, that's the start of the digital empire. They kind of resist this digital empire, use it to make a new world that we cannot control from our ideas of democracy, of...
